title: 2024.02.29 Decision of the AQIU Adjudicatory Body re Marcos JARA
text:
DECISION OF THE
ADJUDICATORY BODY
As per Article 32.3 of the World Aquatics Integrity Code
Decision by:
Anna Peniche (Mexico), Member
Alexandre Miguel Mestre (Portugal), Member
Elliot Saccucci (Canada), Member
In the matter related to:
Mr. Marcos Jara, (Chile), Respondent
Regarding:
Article 2 (a) and (b) of the FINA Code of Conduct and Article C.4 of the FINA
Code of Ethics
29.02.2024
* * * * *

I. Overview
1. The present case relates to the conduct of Mr. Marcos Jara (the “Respondent”
or “Mr. Jara”) who was the President of the Chilean Federation of Aquatics
Sport (“FECHIDA”) from 2019 to 2021.
2. More precisely, in 2020 the Respondent submitted on behalf of the FECHIDA
a tampered invoice and provided false information to World Aquatics
(previously known as FINA) to receive a grant of USD 25.000 linked to the
Olympic Aquatics Support Program of World Aquatics. This invoice was
tampered and used to claim the same financial contribution from both the
National Sport Institute of Chile and from World Aquatics. Likewise in 2021 the
Respondent concealed the fact that costs related to the FECHIDA
representatives’ participation in the South American Championships in
Buenos Aires had already been fully reimbursed through “Asociación de
Deportistas Olímpicos de Chile” (“ADO”). This conduct aimed at obtaining
funds from World Aquatics for the same expenses and again gaining USD
25.000 from the Olympic Aquatics Support Program.
II. Factual background
3. The following summary of the facts does not purport to include every single
contention put forth by the parties during these proceedings. However, the
Adjudicatory Body of the Aquatics Integrity Unit (“AQIU”) has thoroughly
considered any and all evidence and arguments submitted, even if no specific
or detailed reference has been made to those arguments in the following
outline of its positions and in the ensuing discussion on the merits.
A. Corrupt practices related to the 2020 World Aquatics Olympic Aquatics
Support Program
4. In 2020, FECHIDA concluded an agreement with the company Pulpro SpA for
the delivery of various courses in exchange for Pesos 22.800.000.1
5. On 30 June 2020, the Respondent applied to the 2020 Olympic Aquatics
Support Program of World Aquatics. The purpose of this program is to provide
financial support to all of World Aquatics National Member Federations in their
endeavours to develop and foster aquatics at all levels within their territories.
6. In this context, an amount of USD 25,000 was requested from World
Aquatics, specifying that these funds would be used for the project “Escuela
Nacional de Entrenadores” (“National Coaches School”).
7. On 17 August 2020, under a Memorandum between World Aquatics and
FECHIDA, FECHIDA was granted the funding of USD 25.000 for their project
“National Coaches School”.
8. On 27 August 2020, the Respondent signed the Memorandum in his capacity
as President of FECHIDA. By signing the Memorandum, the Respondent
committed to follow the Rules & Regulations of the Olympic Aquatics Support
Programme and also declared that FECHIDA would make accurate and true
use of the FINA Olympic Aquatics Support Programme funds for the projects
1 According to the publicly available sources, Pesos 22.800.000 was approximately USD 28.000
considering the exchange rate from CLP (Chilean Peso) to USD (American dollar) on 5 October 2020.

approved and explained in the Memorandum of 17 August 2020.
9. On 8 September 2020, World Aquatics paid to FECHIDA the first tranche of
USD 17,500.
10. On 21 December 2020, the Respondent, in order to substantiate the
employment of funds and receive the second tranche, submitted the final
report for the 2020 Olympic Aquatics Support Program. As an attachment to
the final report, the Respondent submitted an invoice dated 5 October 2020
of Pesos 22.800.000 (twenty-two million eight hundred thousand pesos)
from Pulpro SpA to FECHIDA.
11. On 9 March 2021, World Aquatics paid to FECHIDA the second tranche of USD
7,500 for a total of USD 25,000.
B. Corrupt practices related to the 2021 World Aquatics Olympic Aquatics
Support Program
12. On 26 November 2020, the Respondent filed another application but this
time for the 2021 Olympic Aquatics Support Program of World Aquatics
specifying that funds demanded from World Aquatics would be used for the
FECHIDA’s "Participacion Sudamericano Adulto 2021” (“Participation in the
South American Championships in Buenos Aires”). The final amount of
demanded funds mentioned in 2021 Application was USD 25.000.
13. On 25 February 2021, in accordance with a Memorandum between World
Aquatics and FECHIDA, FECHIDA was granted the funding of USD 25.000 in
relation to “Participation in the South American Championships in Buenos
Aires”.
14. On the same day, the Respondent signed the 2021 Memorandum in his
capacity as President of FECHIDA. Also in this case, by signing this
Memorandum, the Respondent committed to follow the Rules & Regulations
of the Olympic Aquatics Support Programme and also declared that FECHIDA
will make accurate and true use of the World Aquatics Olympic Aquatics
Support Programme funds for the projects approved and explained in 2021
Memorandum.
15. On 22 March 2021, World Aquatics paid to FECHIDA the first tranche of USD
17,275.
16. On 21 December 2021, the Respondent, in order to substantiate the
employment of funds and receive the second tranche, submitted the final
report for the 2021 Olympic Aquatics Support Program. As an attachment to
the 2021 final report, the Respondent submitted three invoices from
Confederación Argentina de Deportes Acuaticos (Argentine Swimming
Federation) to FECHIDA.
17. On 25 July 2022, based on the information provided in the 2021 final report
and the attached Invoice dated 14 March 2021, Invoice dated 16 March 2021
and Invoice dated 17 March 2021, World Aquatics paid to FECHIDA the second

tranche of USD 6,660 for a total of USD 23,935.2
C. FECHIDA Internal Investigation
18. In November 2021, in view of the misconduct of the Respondent, the
members of FECHIDA convened an extraordinary assembly, which then
resulted in the election of a new president, Mrs. Claudia Molkembuhr (“Mrs.
Molkembuhr” or the “President”).
19. Following her election, the President informed World Aquatics of the situation
mentioning that she would initiate an internal investigation and request an
auditors' report from the company MSI Global Alliance.
20. In this context, on 10 February 2022, the President asked ADO to provide her
with the information regarding funding of the FECHIDA’s participation in the
South American Championships in Buenos Aires.
21. On 21 February 2022, ADO confirmed that funds in relation to the FECHIDA’s
participation in the South American Championships in Buenos Aires were fully
reimbursed by ADO. From the above, it is apparent that FECHIDA received the
funding both from World Aquatics and ADO.
22. On 25 February 2022, a representative of the company Pulpro SpA also
confirmed that the agreement for the "National Coaching School" program
assumed that the funding would be granted by the National Institute of Sport,
and no mention was ever made of any reimbursement from any World
Aquatics program.
23. On 24 May 2022, MSI Global Alliance provided the auditors' certificate.
24. On 2 February 2023, MSI Global Alliance provided the auditors' report.
25. Both the auditors' certificate and the auditors' report conclude that the
invoice of 5 October 2020 from Pulpro SpA was tampered and used to claim
funding from both the National Sport Institute of Chile and from World
Aquatics (for its Olympic Aquatics Support Program).
26. Furthermore, from the excerpt of the FECHIDA’s bank account, it would
appear that the funds received from World Aquatics for the project “National
Coaches School” are untraceable.
27. Therefore, the President informed World Aquatics of the outcome of
investigations conducted as a result of which the above-mentioned
proceedings were initiated by the AQIU.
III. Procedural background
a. Preliminary procedure before the CECO
28. On 8 March 2023, the CECO decided to open proceedings against the
2 USD 225 were deducted from the invoice of 22 March 2021 for a total of USD 17,275 and USD 840
for the Abu Dhabi accommodation were deducted from the invoice of 25 July 2022 for a total of USD
6660.

Respondent for possible violations of:
i. Article C.4 of the Code of Ethics in force at the time of the alleged
violation which prohibits “corrupt practices”.
ii. Article 2 (a) of the Code of Conduct in force at the time of the alleged
violation which prohibits “acts of misbehaviours”.
iii. Article 2 (b) of the Code of Conduct in force at the time of the alleged
violation which prohibits which prohibits “falsification or alteration of
documents and providing false information”.
29. On 25 August 2023, based on all received information and documents,
pursuant to Article 23 of the World Aquatics Integrity Code (“Integrity Code”),
the CECO decided to formally charge the Respondent by means of a notice
of charge (“Notice of Charge”).
30. According to the Notice of Charge and based on the information in his
possession at that time, the CECO determined that a ban of 20 years from
participating in any Aquatics-related activity, including acting as president of
a World Aquatics Member Federation, should be the applicable consequence
in this case.
31. Furthermore, in the Notice of Charge, the Respondent was informed that in
accordance with Article 21 of the Integrity Code, the CECO decided to impose
a provisional suspension on him given that public confidence in the integrity
of the sport of Aquatics was at risk.
32. The provisional suspension has been effective from 25 August 2023 and
prevents the Respondent from participating in any Aquatics-related activity,
including acting as president of a World Aquatics Member Federation.
33. The Respondent was also informed that in accordance with Article 23.3 of the
Integrity Code, he may respond to the Notice of Charge by 8 September 2023
in one of the following ways:
i. Admit the charge and accept a twenty-year ban from taking part in
any aquatics-related activity, including acting as president of a World
Aquatics Member Federation;
ii. Admit the charge, but dispute and/or seek to mitigate all or any of the
potential consequences and have the Adjudicatory Body determine
the consequences and sanctions; or
iii. Deny the charge, and have the Adjudicatory Body determine the
charge and any consequences and sanctions.
34. On 25 August 2023, the Respondent exercised his right under Article 23.3 c)
of the Integrity Code by denying all allegations against him.
35. In brief, the Respondent submitted that he did not present a tampered invoice
or provide false information to World Aquatics, but he merely translated the
invoice in order to meet a formality requirement of World Aquatics. Regarding
the funds allocated to FECHIDA for the South American Championships in
Argentina in 2021, he stated these funds were never used, as it was not certain

they would be obtained and therefore the resources were managed by other
means at the time.
b. Procedure before the Adjudicatory Body
3. On 29 December 2023, the CECO referred the matter to the Adjudicatory
Body.
4. On 4 January 2024, the Adjudicatory Body, afforded Mr. Jara an opportunity
to provide his position on the matter.
5. On 19 January 2024, the Respondent provided his reply to the Adjudicatory
Body, and in summary, he denied the allegations by pointing out that there is
no criminal charge against him in his country and requested an expert's report
on the allegedly manipulated document to establish whether or not it had
actually been altered.
IV. CONSIDERATIONS OF THE ADJUDICATORY BODY
A. Jurisdiction and applicability of the Integrity Code
6. Pursuant to article 4.3 of the Integrity Code: "For matters where the violation
is alleged to have occurred before 1 January 2023 and concerning a person
that has ceased to be subject to the World Aquatics Constitution and/or any
World Aquatics Rules before 1 January 2023, both such person and World
Aquatics shall be entitled to request at the start of the proceedings the
procedure to be conducted in accordance with the previous World Aquatics
(FINA) Code of Ethics, World Aquatics (FINA) Code of Conduct, World Aquatics
(FINA) Rules on the Prevention of the Manipulation of Competitions, and
World Aquatics (FINA) Rules of Conduct Applicable to Bidders".
7. The Respondent was active as president of the FECHIDA and therefore bound
by the FINA Code of Ethics and FINA Code of Conduct in force at the time of
the alleged violation.
8. In accordance with Article 24 of the Integrity Code, the Adjudicatory Body of
the AQIU is responsible for adjudicating cases where a respondent has denied
the charges or requests laid by the CECO.
9. The above shows that the AQIU, and, more precisely, the Adjudicatory Body,
has jurisdiction over the case and is entitled to pass a decision on the basis of
the Integrity Code.
B. Standard of proof
10. The above having been established, the Adjudicatory Body recalled that, as a
general rule, the AQIU will have the burden of establishing that an Integrity
Code Violation has been committed.
11. The standard of proof will be the balance of probabilities. Facts shall be
established by any reliable means. The Panel shall at its own discretion
determine the admissibility, relevance, materiality and weight of the evidence
offered.
12. The principle of strict liability applies. Therefore, violations are punishable

regardless of whether they have been committed intentionally, recklessly,
and/or negligently.
13. Having clarified the foregoing, the Adjudicatory Body proceeded to consider
the merits of the case.
C. Merits of the case
14. Article 2 (a) and (b) of the Code of Conduct stipulates as follows:
“The following incidents or offences shall be subject to the application of this
Code:
a) acts of misbehaviour including but not limited to abusive, violent conduct
in a disturbing, ugly or provocative manner, unjustified interference including
disobedience with obstruction of the orderly conduct of any sporting event
within or outside of the venue(s), malicious alteration, damage or destruction
of property or infliction of physical or mental harm on others;
b) cheating including but not limited to falsification or alteration of birth
certificates, documents of identification or any other document indicating
false age, false nationality or any other false information with the purpose of
obtaining unfair advantage for an official, an athlete or a team:”
15. Article C.4 of the Code of Ethics stipulates as follows:
"Betting on Aquatics and other corrupt practices relating to the sport of
Aquatics by any person being subject to this Code, including improperly
influencing the outcomes and results of an event or competition are
prohibited".
16. The conduct of the Respondent falls under these provisions.
17. By submitting a tampered invoice and providing false information for the
purpose of receiving funds from World Aquatics for the "National Coaches
School" project, which has already been fully reimbursed by the National Sport
Institute of Chile, the Respondent committed corrupt practices, acts of
misbehaviours and falsification or alteration of documents and providing false
information within the meaning of Article C.4 of the Code of Ethics and Article
2 a) and b) of the Code of Conduct.
18. By concealing the fact that FECHIDA's participation in the South American
Championships in Buenos Aires had already been fully reimbursed through
ADO in order to obtain funds from World Aquatics for the same expenses, the
Respondent also committed corrupt practices, acts of misbehaviours and
falsification or alteration of documents and providing false information within
the meaning of Article C.4 of the Code of Ethics and Article 2 a) and b) of the
Code of Conduct. Moreover, the fact that the Respondent stated that it was
not aware of the fate of the funds from World Aquatics does not induce
confidence, especially considering that the Respondent was in a position to
be aware of such matters at the time.
19. On the other hand, the arguments raised by the Respondent in his defence
are irrelevant and can be dismissed in full.

20. The Respondent defends himself against the charge of alteration of the
invoice on the basis that the invoice that was sent to World Aquatics was not
altered but merely translated into English. Respondent further argues that the
translation of the invoice into English was done because all documents
submitted to World Aquatics must be in English and therefore it sought to
comply with those requirements.
21. Respondent's claim that the invoice was merely translated is contradicted by
the file on record. Indeed, even in Spanish, there are two versions of the
invoice, one apparently created for submission to World Aquatics and the
other for submission to the National Sport Institute of Chile. The translation
allegation is also untrue in the sense that the Respondent did not bother to
translate the documents submitted to World Aquatics into English at all times
in the relevant years 2020 and 2021. For example, both the 2020 Application
and the 2021 Application contain sections that are written in Spanish and left
untranslated.
22. Finally, the Respondent does not address the fact that Pulpro SpA claims that
the National Coaches School project should never have been funded by World
Aquatics and that the auditors’ report concludes that the invoice of 5 October
2020 from Pulpro SpA was modified and used to claim funding from both the
National Sport Institute of Chile and from World Aquatics (for its Olympic
Aquatics Support Program).
23. The Respondent makes no comment on the concealment of the fact of the
funding of FECHIDA's participation in the South American Championships in
Buenos Aires through ADO and only states that it was not certain whether
FECHIDA would receive funding from World Aquatics or not. Respondent
further alleges that the funds that FECHIDA ultimately received from World
Aquatics in connection with its participation in the South American
Championships in Buenos Aires remained in a dollar account and nothing was
done with them until he was President of FECHIDA (16 November 2021).
24. The claim that FECHIDA received the funds from World Aquatics and kept
them in its dollar bank account until the time the Respondent was relieved of
his position as President of FECHIDA is in direct contradiction to his previous
allegation when he stated that he did not actually know where the money from
World Aquatics that was paid to cover expenses related to participation in the
South American Championships in Buenos Aires ended up. In this regard, it
seems more like the Respondent is trying to place the blame on the current
FECHIDA management, when he does not present any evidence to support
his allegations. Indeed, since the Respondent, as he himself stated, he did not
know whether or not he would get the funds from World Aquatics at the time
he requested them from the ADO, he should at least have informed World
Aquatics later that the funds were no longer needed because they had been
covered by the ADO, which he never did.
D. Applicable sanction
25. As per Article 33.1 of the Integrity Code, any one or more of the following
sanctions may be imposed for an Integrity Code Violation:
a) a warning as to future conduct;
b) a reprimand;

c) a fine in an amount proportionate to the seriousness of the violation;
d) an order of reimbursement or restitution;
e) a suspension from carrying out specific activities on behalf of World
Aquatics and/or Continental Organisation and/or World Aquatics Member
for a specified period;
f) a period of ineligibility, the length of which is to be determined based on
what is proportionate in the circumstances of the case, taking into account
in particular (i) the nature of the violation(s), (ii) the degree of fault of the
Covered Person, (iii) the harm that the violation(s) has/have done to the
sport, (iv) the need to deter future violations, and (v) any specific
aggravating or mitigating factors; and
g) any other sanction deemed appropriate, including, but not limited to
disqualification of results, annulment of results of any Event, removal from
office, forfeiture of points and/or of quota places and/or of hosting rights,
other loss of privileges, no contact directives, requirement to complete
educational or other programs, and return of World Aquatics awards.
26. In this case, the Adjudicatory Body considers that a suspension for a fixed
period of 20 years from taking part in any Aquatic-related activities under the
auspices of World Aquatics or any of its members, should be the applicable
consequences in this case.
27. In particular, the Adjudicatory Body considers that a more lenient sanction
would not be sufficient to deter future similar violations which have the
potential to cause serious damage to the image of the sport.
28. The Respondent's repeated violations of the Integrity Code cannot be taken
lightly. The Respondent is an experienced official and former President of a
World Aquatics Member. Moreover, the final damage caused by the
Respondent to World Aquatics amounts to USD 50,000.
29. The Respondent further committed the above-described conduct in full
knowledge and with the intent to enrich himself personally at the expense of
World Aquatics.
30. As widely demonstrated indeed, in 2020 the Respondent submitted a
tampered invoice and provided false information to World Aquatics to claim
the same grant of USD 25.000 from both the National Sport Institute of Chile
and from World Aquatics for the Olympic Aquatics Support Program. This is
well documented in the Auditors’ Certificate:
“Due to the request from the Chilean Federation of Aquatics Sports dated
April 5th, 2022, the following submissions made by said entity were reviewed
and audited:
a) Submission No. 1 2020 for the 2000030586 “Capacitación Nacional
FECHIDA 2020” project, without signature from the person in charge, and run
by the National Sports Institute
b) Submission made for project CHI 2020, dated December 21st 2020, signed

by Marcos Jara Montecino, President of FECHIDA, addressed to the National
Swimming Federation.
Based upon the review and auditing of the documents that support the listed
proceedings, it is certified that the following inconsistencies or observations
have been detected:
- The same accounting document has been included in both proceedings and
submissions: Non-taxable or exempt invoice No. 3, issued by Capacitaciones
Pulpro SpA. RUT 77.189.514-K, dated October 5th, 2020 for $22,800,000.
- Different annotations were included for the same invoice, despite it being a
tax document that must not be altered”.
31. Likewise in 2021 the Respondent claimed funds from both ADO and from
World Aquatics for the same expenses and again gaining USD 25.000 from
the Olympic Aquatics Support Program. This is clearly indicated in the e-mail
from ADO to the President of 21 February 2022:
“At the South American Championship in Argentina, the resources were given
in their totality to Mr. Marcos Jara, from our Exchange House to finance food,
lodging, PCR and other services”.
32. Therefore, the Respondent's conduct must be condemned in every way, and
it must be ensured that such actions are strongly discouraged.
33. Considering the above, the Adjudicatory Body shall impose on the
Respondent a suspension for a fixed period of 20 years from taking part in
any Aquatic-related activities on behalf of World Aquatics and/or
Continental Organisation and/or World Aquatics Member and/or recognised
body. Such suspension shall commence on the date on which the
Respondent was provisionally suspended, thus on 25 August 2023.

I. DECISION OF THE ADJUDICATORY BODY
(i) The Respondent has violated Article 2 (a) and (b) of the Code of
Conduct and Article C.4 of the Code of Ethics.
(ii) The Respondent is sanctioned with a 20-year period of ineligibility
from taking part in any Aquatic-related activities on behalf of World
Aquatics and/or Continental Organisation and/or World Aquatics
Member and/or recognised body.
(iii) The Respondent is sanctioned with a fine of USD 50,000 equivalent
to the amount that has been misappropriated from World Aquatics.
This sum shall be paid directly by the Respondent. Failure to pay the
fine shall permanently prevent the Respondent from taking part in
any Aquatic-related activities on behalf of World Aquatics and/or
Continental Organisation and/or World Aquatics Member and/or
recognised body.
(iv) As per Article 35 of the World Aquatics Integrity Code, this decision
can be appealed to CAS within twenty-one (21) calendar days of the
appealing Party’s receipt of the written reasoned decision in
question by email.
The Panel of the Adjudicatory Body of the Aquatics Integrity Unit:
Anna Peniche Alexandre Miguel Mestre Elliot Saccucci
